[STRUCTURAL DECOUPLING & RIGIDITY CONTRACT]
- GEOMETRY LOCK: Treat all architectural geometry from the seed image as an immutable physical frame. Every column, window recess, sash mullion, cornice, balustrade, and ashlar stone course must remain razor-sharp and structurally intact. DO NOT melt, smooth, smear, or erase building elements.
- OPTICAL DEPTH: Render in pin-sharp deep focus / infinite depth of field (f/11 equivalent). Zero tilt-shift, zero lens blur across foreground and background.
- ILLUMINATION REPAINT: Completely discard seed image baked-in luminance. Repaint all cast shadows, highlights, and ambient bounce strictly according to the solar vector below.
- CANOPY RIGIDITY: Render foliage with distinct individual leaf clusters and crisp branch morphology, not smooth airbrushed masses.

[SOLAR & ATMOSPHERIC LIGHTING OVERRIDE]
NOCTURNAL / TWILIGHT RELIGHTING DIRECTIVE (2000K Nocturnal / Night Scene):
- SUN POSITION: Sun is below the horizon (Elevation -9.3°). ZERO direct solar exposure.
- FACADE ILLUMINATION: Complete absence of direct sunlight. All facades, spires, domes, and roofs must have ZERO harsh directional sun highlights.
- SHADOW OVERWRITE RULE: MANDATORY: Completely extinguish all baked-in daytime sunlight and directional shadows. Render all stone surfaces in soft, flat, ambient nocturnal skylight with subtle contact occlusion.
- CAST SHADOW DIRECTION: No solar cast shadows exist.
- WEATHER/SKY: 100% overcast cloud cover with soft, omnidirectional 6500K diffuse skylight and zero harsh shadow lines.

[SCENE GEOMETRY & AUTHENTIC LITHICS]
Medium format 6x7 documentary architectural photograph, wide eye-level vista along London Street terminating at Drummond Place circus, Edinburgh New Town. Flanking Neo-Classical Georgian terraced tenements built in pale buff Craigleith quartzose sandstone, displaying plumb vertical alignments, polished fine-jointed ashlar ashlar facades, V-jointed rusticated ground floors, and crisp continuous eaves cornices with blocking courses. Symmetrical fenestration grids of white-painted 6-over-6 timber sash-and-case windows set deeply within crisp rectangular stone reveals.
